description.narrative:
As one of the recipients of Voice Now Us Award, Motherhen is committed to addressing the GBV menace in Gombe <(>&<)> some parts of Borno State, Nigeria, within the 12months life span of the project. GBV is a recurring problem in Gombe State and unfortunately mostof the rape cases rarely ever make it to court. Families of the victims/survivors are intimidated into dropping the case and usually, there are no form of support for the victims/survivors, but rather stigmatization, thereby encouraging the culture ofsilence.
Toaddress this gap, Motherhen proposes the “YAKI DA CIN ZARFIN JINSI'' – ‘War Against GBV in Gombe <(>&<)> Southern Borno States’ campaign aimed at ending violence against women <(>&<)> girls in the 2 States through community sensitization and economic empowerment of the rightsholders. The three objectives of the project are as follows:
1. Launch the “YAKI DA CIN ZARFIN JINSI'' – ‘War Against GBV in Gombe <(>&<)> Southern Borno States’ campaign to create awareness at community level, on Gender and Economicjustice 2. To create safe space and boost their economy power of the rightsholders, by linking them to market opportunities 3. Engage the community gatekeepers to ensure that actions are taken to mitigate VAWG risks and ensure full utilization of the existing referral pathways forreporting suspected cases of VAWG
In the past, Motherhen have been able to set up safe spaces for victims of gender-based violencewhere they are provided with shelter and taught skills and then re-integrated back into thecommunities- this will be adopted in current project with ease. They will also be adopting a Participatory Rural Appraisal and Participatory Learning and Action approaches in identifying and handling these issues. They will use community vanguards set upin their target communities to visit families and attend to cases sometimes independently.
The change they would like to see is the eradication of violence against women <(>&<)> girls in Gombe <(>&<)> Southern part of Borno State, because survivors are protected and provided with means of getting justice.

participating-org.narrative:
Motherhen Development Foundation (MDF) is a Non-Governmental, Non- Political, Non- Religious Organization and cuts across ethnic groups in Nigeria. MDF is geared toward improving the quality of life in communities and families, especially the Poor of thePoorest (PoP). MDF is dedicated to the upliftment of women and young people, especially the underserved and the unsung women and youths in our rural communities by identifying the issues affecting public health, gaps in basic education, environmental hazards, socio-economic, political, leadership development, capacity building, and specialized vocational education training, rural development initiative(RDI).
MDF is also an umbrella body to 125 Co-operatives and Community-Based Organizations CBOs whose members are in various (un)skilled professions. Agencies can take advantage of our spread and partner with MDF to sensitize rural communities on various projects. MDF provides social development platforms in rural communities through education and income generation skills that are eco-friendly to improve the lives and social standing of communities, these have ripple effects on health care, education, and economic development of the nation.
MDF has been able to break the huge barriers that exist in language, religion, culture, and convenience by designing a localized approach that allows women and youths of the same or different backgrounds to reach out to their peers thus creating massive extension services which can be deployed in marketing any product.
● VISION: envision a stable, prosperous, and vibrantcommunities characterized by good governance; economic prosperity; democracy; good environment/health; human rights; and social justice
● MISSION: Utilizing our potential, building strongercommunities, and strengthening the knowledge base of women, girls, and youths through an increase in providing platforms on making informed decisions about improving livelihood.
● CORE VALUE: We value integrity, honesty and recognize our unique contribution We welcome all equally; we respect and are reliable We value accountability and promote quality through continued reflection and improvement We use a person-centered approach, realizing individual potential and allow room for innovations We areresponsible and we partner with like minds in our field of endeavor
AIMS AND OBJECTIVES: • To provide responsive, supportive, and innovative services to women • To be a platform for community development • To grow and sustain an effective organization
Geographic coverage: MDF operates in at least one State of the 6 zones in Nigeria with a full presence in the Northeast (Adamawa, Taraba, Bauchi Gombe, Yobe, and Borno States)
GOVERNANCE: The Board of Trustees is the highest policy-making bodythat governs MDF. The Board approves the organization’s strategies and is responsible for ensuring that the organization's policies and strategies are in keeping with its mission. The Board is made up of women and men of great reputation who have distinguished themselves in various fields of endeavor and are responsible for the establishment of meaningful policies for running the organization.
MANAGEMENT BOARD: The organization is ably headed by a FEMALE Executive Director who is the Lead, and supportedby the Director of Finance, Director of Programmes/project specialist, Director of Administration, and other support staff.
